locator: §2.5, 'we can capture the content of the judgment that action A is permissible by specifying the set of world-norm pairs with which it is incompatible'
interpretation: Gibbard's norm-expressivism (1990) and plan-expressivism (2003, fact-prac worlds): the content of a normative judgment is the set of world-norm (later world-plan) pairs it rules out, and complex sentences get their contents by combining these. The content belongs to the judgment a sentence expresses, whatever the occurrence, so this is a claim of constant-meaning expressivism. Gibbard's variant of the theory. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
